A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, algorithms, and complete Appendices A and B are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A report original PINN optimization experiments on 5d, 10d, and 100d Poisson problems, including convergence, randomization, and effective-dimension analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original Poisson experiments and adds Heat and logarithmic Fokker–Planck results, plus measured Nyström runtime and memory comparisons in Table 1.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 replaces the written SPRING update eta_k*phi_k with phi_k*min(eta_k, sqrt(C)/||phi_k||), introducing a norm constraint C. This is a limited revision to the stated procedure; the Woodbury, momentum, and Nyström computations otherwise remain intact. The PDFs do not establish whether the earlier implementation already used this constraint.

E1.justification: v2 adds a 4+1d Heat equation and a 9+1d logarithmic Fokker–Planck equation while retaining the Poisson problems, including the appendix-only 10d case. This substantially broadens evaluation to time-dependent problems and a nonlinear differential equation in logarithmic coordinates.

E2.justification: Figures 4, 5, 9, and 15 remove the ENGD (Naive) or SPRING (Naive) comparator curves. Figure 3 adds numerical KFAC reference levels, including for 5d Poisson; v1 already discussed KFAC performance in its 100d comparison. These are reference results attributed to prior work, with no newly run KFAC experiments documented.

E3.justification: The existing evaluation framework is retained, with new Heat and log-Fokker–Planck runs using 3000s and 6000s budgets. Appendix B replaces the N=3500, S=1750 benchmark description with N=5000, sketches spanning 20–80%, and peak-memory measurement. A.4 and Figure 13 change Bayesian search to random search; this reported correction does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds a focused scaling analysis testing how runtime, memory, and GPU acceleration depend on sketch size. Appendices A.5–A.6 extend momentum and fixed-learning-rate versus line-search comparisons to the new PDEs. The existing effective-dimension analysis and principal randomization conclusions are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report selected hyperparameter-search runs and average benchmark timings over 100 runs after 10 warm-up runs. Neither adds seed-based variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The increase from over 3000 to over 4500 total training runs describes expanded experimental effort, not a new uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: Figures 3 and 16–19 add Heat and log-Fokker–Planck convergence results, including a reported order-of-magnitude SPRING advantage over the plotted KFAC reference on log-Fokker–Planck. New Table 1 reports 13.29–65.41× Nyström speedups and lower peak memory across four sketch sizes. Naive-variant results are removed from four figures; most retained Poisson curves are unchanged. These additions are not same-setting v1-to-v2 performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix A.6 adds the mathematical transformation of the general Fokker–Planck equation under q=log(p), including the transformed differential operator. The existing Woodbury and SPRING derivations remain unchanged, and no new convergence theorem or proof is introduced. Algorithm 2's regularization notation is clarified without changing its factorization steps.

C1.justification: The three central methodological contributions and the abstract's 75× acceleration claim remain unchanged. The conclusion adds claims of competitive Heat-equation performance against KFAC and an order-of-magnitude error advantage on log-Fokker–Planck, modestly extending the stated empirical contribution.

C2.justification: New discussion explains why differing sampling distributions permit transferring VMC techniques to PINNs, qualifies Woodbury's quadratic batch-size scaling against KFAC's linear scaling, and attributes disagreement with McKay et al. to comparison against the stronger ENGD-W baseline. The existing limitations concerning late-stage accuracy, high-dimensional randomization, and adaptive rank selection remain.

D1.justification: Appendices A.5–A.6 add substantial specifications for the new experiments: equations, initial and boundary conditions, sampling, architectures, time budgets, search spaces, and selected hyperparameters. Algorithm 1 exposes C without specifying its numerical value. Appendix B revises benchmark details but drops the earlier parameter-size and random-matrix construction description. Hardware, precision, and the prospective implementation-release statement remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds McKay et al., Near-optimal sketchy natural gradients for physics-informed neural networks, and explicitly contrasts its randomization findings with comparisons against ENGD-W. The broader positioning remains intact. Consolidating the duplicate Jacot et al. references does not remove a distinct cited work.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the section sequence are retained. Changes include focused explanatory paragraphs, expanded experimental setup and conclusion passages, new appendix subsections, a rewritten Appendix B, and updated affiliation, contact, acknowledgment, and conference text.

P2.justification: Figure 3 expands from two to four panels and gains dashed KFAC reference levels. Four new appendix figures and Table 1 substantially expand the empirical displays. Figures 4, 5, 9, and 15 are redrawn without Naive curves and their legend entries, while most other plots retain their content.

improvement.justification: The new PDE families substantially address v1's Poisson-only validation, while Table 1 supplies concrete runtime and memory evidence where v1's benchmarking appendix provided only a setup description. These changes materially strengthen support for general applicability and GPU efficiency. Inconsistent Heat network-size labels, the unspecified norm-constraint value, and prose still describing removed randomized comparisons limit reproducibility and clarity, but do not outweigh those gains.
